title: Engine Lifecycle and Checkpoints
summary: Start, restart, query, and mark a recovery anchor so the core engine lifecycle stays demonstrable while maintenance work keeps moving.
whySQLiteFallsShort: SQLite persistence is file-centric, but SydraDB combines engine lifecycle, ingest/query, and CAS-backed recovery anchors in one storage model.
This makes restart behavior and maintenance history part of the product demonstration, not a side exercise around a generic embedded database file.
Engine work can be validated end-to-end with real restart and checkpoint flows as the core continues to change.

steps.title: Start the engine
steps.summary: Bring the edge-east server online in its fresh scenario workspace.

steps.title: Query before restart
steps.summary: Confirm the seeded points are visible from the live engine before any restart happens.

steps.title: Restart the engine
steps.summary: Restart the live process so recovery and replay behavior become visible in the same workflow.

steps.title: Query after restart
steps.summary: Re-run the range query after restart to prove the engine still serves the expected points.

steps.title: Create a named recovery anchor
steps.summary: Mark the current head with a Git-like branch so later engine work has a known-good state to compare and restore.

steps.summary: Confirm the repository now exposes the lifecycle anchor alongside heads/main.
